docs.text: FLIR camera control via Bonsai for murine shift work experiments

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: pip install msw_flir_bonsai

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
# Find Bonsai.exe path on the acquisition machine
msw-flir find-bonsai

# List connected FLIR cameras and their indices
msw-flir list-cameras --driver flycap

# Run a 5-second test recording from camera 0
msw-flir test-record --cam-index 0 --fps 30 --duration 5

# Launch two cameras for a full session (blocks until Ctrl+C)
msw-flir run D:\DATA\video mouse001__20260524 --n-cameras 2 --fps 60

For Python API usage, timestamp preprocessing, and barcode alignment, see the Usage section. For MSW setup YAML configuration, see the murineshiftwork setup docs.

class BonsaiCameraRunner:
    """Manage a single Bonsai camera acquisition subprocess.

    Args:
        bonsai_exe: Path to ``Bonsai.exe``. Falls back to ``BONSAI_EXE`` env var.
        workflow: Workflow stem name (without ``.bonsai``),
            e.g. ``"run-flir-flycap-1cam"``.
        acqdir: Full path to the pre-created video_flir acquisition directory.
        cam_basename: Pre-computed file stem for this camera, e.g.
            ``"mouse01__dt__video_flir.mswflir.top.0"``.  The workflow appends
            ``.avi`` / ``.timestamps.csv`` to produce output filenames.
        cam_index: Camera SDK enumeration index (``cam1idx`` workflow property).
        cam_serial: Camera serial number (``cam1serial``, Spinnaker only). When
            set, the Spinnaker node selects the camera by serial and ignores
            the index; empty keeps index selection.
        fps: Target frame rate (FlyCapture only; ignored for Spinnaker).  Frame
            rate should be configured in camera non-volatile memory; only pass
            this for an explicit CLI override.
        driver: ``"flycap"`` or ``"spinnaker"``: controls which properties are passed.
        extra_props: Additional ``-p key=value`` pairs forwarded to Bonsai CLI.
        startup_timeout: Seconds to wait for the subprocess to start before raising.
        start_timeout: Seconds after launch for the first frame to reach the
            ``.avi`` (:meth:`check_started`).
        retry_delay: Seconds to wait before the single relaunch after Bonsai
            exited without a frame (:meth:`check_started`); None disables it.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        workflow: str,
        acqdir: str | Path,
        cam_basename: str,
        cam_index: int = 0,
        fps: int | None = None,
        driver: str = "flycap",
        cam_serial: str = "",
        bonsai_exe: str | Path | None = None,
        extra_props: dict[str, str] | None = None,
        startup_timeout: float = _STARTUP_TIMEOUT,
        start_timeout: float = _START_TIMEOUT_S,
        retry_delay: float | None = _EARLY_EXIT_RETRY_DELAY_S,
    ) -> None:
        self._bonsai_exe = _find_bonsai_exe(bonsai_exe)
        self._workflow_path = workflow_path(workflow)
        self._acqdir = str(acqdir)
        self._cam_basename = cam_basename
        self._cam_index = cam_index
        self._cam_serial = cam_serial
        self._fps = fps
        self._driver = driver
        self._extra_props = extra_props or {}
        self._startup_timeout = startup_timeout
        self._start_timeout = start_timeout
        self._avi_before: tuple[int, int] | None = None
        self._retry_delay = retry_delay
        self._exited_unexpectedly = False
        # The monitor stays quiet while check_started runs and about an exit
        # the check has already logged, so one failure is logged exactly once.
        self._checking = False
        self._exit_reported: subprocess.Popen | None = None

        self._process: subprocess.Popen | None = None
        self._monitor_thread: threading.Thread | None = None
        self._stopped = threading.Event()
        self._stop_file: Path | None = None
        self._layout_file: Path | None = None
        self._started_at = 0.0

    def _build_cmd(self) -> list[str]:
        """Assemble the Bonsai subprocess command list with all -p property flags."""
        props: dict[str, str] = {
            "acqdir": f'"{self._acqdir}"',
            "cam_basename": f'"{self._cam_basename}"',
            "cam1idx": str(self._cam_index),
        }
        if self._driver == "flycap":
            if self._fps is not None:
                props["cam1fps"] = str(self._fps)
            props["cam1ts"] = "True"
            props["cam1framecounter"] = "True"
        elif self._driver == "spinnaker" and self._cam_serial:
            props["cam1serial"] = self._cam_serial

        props.update(self._extra_props)

        cmd = [
            self._bonsai_exe,
            str(self._workflow_path),
            "--start",
            "--no-editor",
        ]
        layout = self._preview_layout()
        if layout is not None:
            cmd += ["--visualizer-layout", str(layout)]
        for key, value in props.items():
            cmd += ["-p", f"{key}={value}"]
        return cmd

    def _preview_layout(self) -> Path | None:
        """Per-camera copy of the workflow's ``.bonsai.layout`` (live preview window).

        The window is shifted right by camera index so several cameras sit side by
        side. Returns None when the workflow has no layout file.
        """
        template = Path(f"{self._workflow_path}.layout")
        if not template.exists():
            return None
        x = 40 + self._cam_index * 660
        xml = template.read_text(encoding="utf-8").replace(
            "<Location><X>40</X>", f"<Location><X>{x}</X>", 1
        )
        out = (
            Path(tempfile.gettempdir())
            / f"msw-bonsai-{os.getpid()}-cam{self._cam_index}.layout"
        )
        out.write_text(xml, encoding="utf-8")
        self._layout_file = out
        return out

    def start(self) -> None:
        """Launch the Bonsai subprocess and begin background monitoring."""
        if self._process is not None and self._process.poll() is None:
            raise RuntimeError("BonsaiCameraRunner is already running.")

        cmd = self._build_cmd()
        logging.info(f"[BonsaiCamera cam{self._cam_index}] Starting: {' '.join(cmd)}")
        self._write_metadata()

        self._stopped.clear()
        self._exited_unexpectedly = False
        self._avi_before = self._avi_stat()
        # Graceful stop: Extensions/key-ctrl-stop.bonsai polls this file and
        # completes the stream once it exists, so the AVI/CSV writers flush and
        # close and Bonsai exits.
        self._stop_file = (
            Path(tempfile.gettempdir())
            / f"msw-bonsai-{os.getpid()}-cam{self._cam_index}.stop"
        )
        self._stop_file.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        self._process = subprocess.Popen(
            cmd,
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            env={
                **os.environ,
                "MSW_BONSAI_STOP_FILE": str(self._stop_file),
                "MSW_BONSAI_PARENT_PID": str(os.getpid()),
            },
            # Own process group: a Ctrl+C in the caller's console must not kill
            # Bonsai before the caller has shut down and requested a clean stop.
            creationflags=getattr(subprocess, "CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP", 0),
        )

        self._started_at = time.monotonic()
        self._monitor_thread = threading.Thread(
            target=self._monitor,
            args=(self._process,),
            daemon=True,
            name=f"bonsai-cam{self._cam_index}-monitor",
        )
        self._monitor_thread.start()
        logging.info(
            f"[BonsaiCamera cam{self._cam_index}] Process started "
            f"(pid={self._process.pid})"
        )

    def _write_metadata(self) -> None:
        """Write the per-camera metadata file (driver, CSV layout); never raises."""
        from msw_flir_bonsai.metadata import camera_metadata, write_camera_metadata

        meta = camera_metadata(
            driver=self._driver,
            workflow=self._workflow_path.stem,
            cam_index=self._cam_index,
            fps=self._fps,
        )
        write_camera_metadata(self._acqdir, self._cam_basename, meta)

    @property
    def avi_path(self) -> Path:
        """The video file the workflow writes: ``<acqdir>/<cam_basename>.avi``."""
        return Path(self._acqdir) / f"{self._cam_basename}.avi"

    def _avi_stat(self) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
        try:
            st = self.avi_path.stat()
        except OSError:
            return None
        return st.st_size, st.st_mtime_ns

    def _start_status(self) -> str | None:
        """``""`` once the first frame is written, a failure reason, or None."""
        stat = self._avi_stat()
        # a file left from an earlier run (same size and mtime) is not a frame
        if stat is not None and stat[0] > 0 and stat != self._avi_before:
            return ""
        assert self._process is not None
        rc = self._process.poll()
        if rc is not None:
            self._exit_reported = self._process  # check_started logs it
            age = time.monotonic() - self._started_at
            return (
                f"Bonsai cam{self._cam_index} exited {age:.1f} s after launch "
                f"without a frame (returncode={rc}): camera missing or in use, "
                "or the workflow failed"
            )
        return None

    def check_started(
        self,
        timeout: float | None = None,
        expect_present: bool = True,
        deadline: float | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Block until the first frame is in the ``.avi``; raise if it never is.

        Polls every 0.25 s. The start fails when Bonsai exits first (at any
        time; its return code is 0 either way) or when ``timeout`` (default
        ``start_timeout``) passes with Bonsai alive but no frame; Bonsai is
        then stopped. After an exit without a frame Bonsai is relaunched once
        after ``retry_delay`` s, because the camera may not be released yet,
        unless ``expect_present=False`` (the caller knows the camera is
        missing, so the relaunch would fail too). The relaunch gets a fresh
        ``timeout``.

        Args:
            timeout: Seconds from launch to wait for the first frame.
            expect_present: False skips the relaunch.
            deadline: ``time.monotonic()`` deadline for the first attempt,
                shared by several cameras; overrides ``timeout`` for it.

        Raises:
            BonsaiStartError: No frame: Bonsai exited (on the relaunch too)
                or the timeout passed.
        """
        if self._process is None:
            return
        self._checking = True
        try:
            self._check_started(timeout, expect_present, deadline)
        finally:
            self._checking = False

    def _check_started(
        self, timeout: float | None, expect_present: bool, deadline: float | None
    ) -> None:
        if timeout is None:
            timeout = self._start_timeout
        if deadline is None:
            deadline = self._started_at + timeout
        msg = self._wait_first_frame(deadline)
        if msg is None:
            return
        exited = msg.startswith("Bonsai")  # a timeout is never relaunched
        if exited and not expect_present:
            msg += " (no relaunch: camera not detected)"
        if not exited or not expect_present or self._retry_delay is None:
            logging.error(f"[BonsaiCamera cam{self._cam_index}] {msg}")
            raise BonsaiStartError(msg)
        logging.warning(
            f"[BonsaiCamera cam{self._cam_index}] {msg}; attempt 1 of 2, "
            f"relaunching in {self._retry_delay:g} s"
        )
        time.sleep(self._retry_delay)
        self.start()
        msg = self._wait_first_frame(self._started_at + timeout)
        if msg is None:
            logging.info(f"[BonsaiCamera cam{self._cam_index}] Relaunch recording")
            return
        logging.error(f"[BonsaiCamera cam{self._cam_index}] {msg}; attempt 2 of 2")
        raise BonsaiStartError(f"{msg} (after one relaunch)")

    def _wait_first_frame(self, deadline: float) -> str | None:
        """None once a frame is written, else the failure reason.

        Exit reasons start with ``"Bonsai"``; on a timeout Bonsai is stopped
        and the reason starts with ``"no frame"``.
        """
        while True:
            status = self._start_status()
            if status == "":
                return None
            if status is not None:
                return status
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                self.stop()
                return (
                    f"no frame from cam{self._cam_index} in {self.avi_path.name} "
                    "before the start timeout; Bonsai stopped"
                )
            time.sleep(_START_POLL_S)

    def _monitor(self, proc: subprocess.Popen) -> None:
        """Poll ``proc`` in a daemon thread and record an exit before stop.

        Takes the process it watches: after a relaunch the old thread must not
        flag the new process. While check_started runs, and for an exit it
        has logged, the monitor only flags the exit; otherwise it logs it.
        """
        while not self._stopped.is_set() and proc is self._process:
            rc = proc.poll()
            if rc is not None:
                if not self._stopped.is_set() and proc is self._process:
                    self._exited_unexpectedly = True
                    if not self._checking and proc is not self._exit_reported:
                        logging.error(
                            f"[BonsaiCamera cam{self._cam_index}] "
                            f"Process exited unexpectedly (returncode={rc})"
                        )
                break
            time.sleep(0.5)

    def stop(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> None:
        """Gracefully terminate the Bonsai subprocess."""
        if self._process is None:
            return
        self._stopped.set()
        if self._process.poll() is None:
            logging.info(f"[BonsaiCamera cam{self._cam_index}] Requesting stop")
            if self._stop_file is not None:
                self._stop_file.touch()
            try:
                self._process.wait(timeout=timeout)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                logging.warning(
                    f"[BonsaiCamera cam{self._cam_index}] Stop timed out; killing"
                )
                if os.name == "nt":
                    # Bonsai.exe relaunches itself as a child worker; kill() would only
                    # kill the launcher and orphan the worker. Kill the whole tree.
                    subprocess.run(
                        ["taskkill", "/F", "/T", "/PID", str(self._process.pid)],
                        capture_output=True,
                    )
                else:
                    self._process.kill()
                self._process.wait(timeout=5.0)
        for f in (self._stop_file, self._layout_file):
            if f is not None:
                f.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    def wait(self, timeout: float | None = None) -> int | None:
        """Block until the subprocess exits. Returns the return code."""
        if self._process is None:
            return None
        try:
            return self._process.wait(timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return None

    @property
    def exited_unexpectedly(self) -> bool:
        """True if Bonsai exited before :meth:`stop` was requested.

        Bonsai exits 0 when it cannot record, so this, not the return code,
        tells a caller that the recording failed. Check it before :meth:`stop`.
        """
        if self._exited_unexpectedly:
            return True
        return (
            self._process is not None
            and not self._stopped.is_set()
            and self._process.poll() is not None
        )

    @property
    def is_running(self) -> bool:
        """True if the subprocess exists and has not yet exited."""
        return self._process is not None and self._process.poll() is None

    @property
    def pid(self) -> int | None:
        """OS process ID of the Bonsai subprocess, or None if not started."""
        return self._process.pid if self._process else None

class MultiCameraRunner:
    """Launch and manage multiple independent camera subprocesses.

    Each camera is an independent :class:`BonsaiCameraRunner`.  A crash in one
    camera does not propagate to others.  Cameras are stopped in parallel on
    :meth:`stop`.

    Args:
        runners: Pre-constructed :class:`BonsaiCameraRunner` instances.
    """

    def __init__(self, runners: list[BonsaiCameraRunner]) -> None:
        self._runners = runners

    @classmethod
    def from_config(
        cls,
        acqdir: str | Path,
        cam_basenames: list[str],
        driver: str,
        fps: int | None = None,
        bonsai_exe: str | Path | None = None,
        workflow: str = "",
    ) -> MultiCameraRunner:
        """Build one BonsaiCameraRunner per camera using the 1-cam workflow.

        Each camera runs in its own subprocess.  The 1-cam workflow is used so
        each Bonsai process owns exactly one camera: a crash in one does not
        affect the others.

        Args:
            acqdir: Pre-created video_flir acquisition directory.
            cam_basenames: One pre-computed basename per camera (index order).
            driver: ``"flycap"`` or ``"spinnaker"``.
            fps: Optional FlyCapture frame-rate override.
            bonsai_exe: Path to Bonsai.exe (falls back to BONSAI_EXE env var).
            workflow: Workflow stem; auto-derived as ``run-flir-{driver}-1cam``
                if empty.
        """
        resolved_workflow = workflow or f"run-flir-{driver}-1cam"
        runners = [
            BonsaiCameraRunner(
                workflow=resolved_workflow,
                acqdir=acqdir,
                cam_basename=cam_basenames[i],
                cam_index=i,
                fps=fps,
                driver=driver,
                bonsai_exe=bonsai_exe,
            )
            for i in range(len(cam_basenames))
        ]
        return cls(runners)

    def start(self, timeout: float | None = None, expect_present: bool = True) -> None:
        """Start all camera subprocesses, then wait for every first frame.

        The cameras are waited for in parallel against one shared deadline
        (``timeout`` from now, default each runner's ``start_timeout``).
        ``timeout=0`` skips the wait. ``expect_present`` is passed to
        :meth:`BonsaiCameraRunner.check_started`.

        Raises:
            BonsaiStartError: A camera wrote no frame; all cameras are stopped
                before raising.
        """
        for runner in self._runners:
            runner.start()
        if timeout is not None and timeout <= 0:
            return
        deadline = None if timeout is None else time.monotonic() + timeout
        failed: list[str] = []

        def wait(runner: BonsaiCameraRunner) -> None:
            try:
                runner.check_started(
                    timeout, expect_present=expect_present, deadline=deadline
                )
            except BonsaiStartError as e:
                failed.append(str(e))

        threads = [
            threading.Thread(target=wait, args=(r,), daemon=True) for r in self._runners
        ]
        for t in threads:
            t.start()
        for t in threads:
            t.join()
        if failed:
            self.stop()
            raise BonsaiStartError("; ".join(failed))

    def stop(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> None:
        """Stop all camera subprocesses in parallel and wait for them to exit."""
        threads = []
        for runner in self._runners:
            t = threading.Thread(
                target=runner.stop, kwargs={"timeout": timeout}, daemon=True
            )
            t.start()
            threads.append(t)
        for t in threads:
            t.join(timeout=timeout + 2)

    @property
    def all_running(self) -> bool:
        """True if every camera subprocess is still active."""
        return all(r.is_running for r in self._runners)

    @property
    def exited_unexpectedly(self) -> bool:
        """True if any camera's Bonsai exited before stop was requested."""
        return any(r.exited_unexpectedly for r in self._runners)

    @property
    def any_running(self) -> bool:
        """True if at least one camera subprocess is still active."""
        return any(r.is_running for r in self._runners)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._runners)

    def __iter__(self):
        return iter(self._runners)

def probe_cameras(driver: str, timeout: float = 10.0) -> ProbeResult:
    """Find the connected cameras for ``driver``, never loading a DLL here.

    Tries the SDK in a child process, then the USB device list, then gives up
    with source ``"none"``. Errors of the failed sources are joined in
    ``error``. Blocks for at most about ``2 * timeout`` seconds.

    Returns:
        The first source that answered. Never raises.
    """
    if driver not in DRIVERS:
        return ProbeResult(driver, error=f"unknown driver {driver!r}")
    sdk = _probe_in_child(driver, timeout)
    if sdk.source == "sdk":
        return sdk
    usb = probe_usb(driver, timeout)
    errors = [e for e in (sdk.error, usb.error) if e]
    usb.error = "; ".join(errors)
    return usb

units are objects with index, name and an optional serial (msw-core CameraUnit). The plan keeps their order.

  • Source "none": warn and launch by configured index (Spinnaker still gets configured serials).
  • No serials configured: require count >= max(index) + 1.
  • Serials with source "sdk": every serial must be connected. FlyCapture launches at the serial's index; Spinnaker passes the serial to Bonsai. Cameras without a serial keep their index, which must exist and not collide with a serial-resolved one.
  • Serials with source "usb": require count >= len(units) and every serial connected. USB gives no index order, so FlyCapture keeps the configured index (warning).

Raises: CameraMismatchError: Cameras are missing, a serial is not connected, or two cameras resolve to the same index.

def resolve_camera_units(
    units: Sequence[Any], driver: str, probe: ProbeResult
) -> list[CameraLaunch]:
    """Turn configured cameras and a probe into the launch plan.

    ``units`` are objects with ``index``, ``name`` and an optional ``serial``
    (msw-core ``CameraUnit``). The plan keeps their order.

    - Source ``"none"``: warn and launch by configured index (Spinnaker still
      gets configured serials).
    - No serials configured: require ``count >= max(index) + 1``.
    - Serials with source ``"sdk"``: every serial must be connected. FlyCapture
      launches at the serial's index; Spinnaker passes the serial to Bonsai.
      Cameras without a serial keep their index, which must exist and not
      collide with a serial-resolved one.
    - Serials with source ``"usb"``: require ``count >= len(units)`` and every
      serial connected. USB gives no index order, so FlyCapture keeps the
      configured index (warning).

    Raises:
        CameraMismatchError: Cameras are missing, a serial is not connected,
            or two cameras resolve to the same index.
    """
    plan = [
        CameraLaunch(
            name=getattr(u, "name", "") or "",
            index=int(u.index),
            serial=_norm(getattr(u, "serial", "")),
        )
        for u in units
    ]
    pass_serial = driver == "spinnaker"
    if not plan:
        return plan
    if probe.source == "none":
        log.warning(
            f"Camera probe unavailable ({probe.error or 'no source'}): "
            "launching by configured index"
        )
        return _finish(plan, pass_serial)

    count = probe.count or 0
    label = f"{count} {driver} camera(s) found via {probe.source}"
    if not any(c.serial for c in plan):
        needed = max(c.index for c in plan) + 1
        if count < needed:
            raise CameraMismatchError(
                f"setup needs {needed} camera(s) (highest index {needed - 1}); {label}"
            )
        return _finish(plan, pass_serial)

    if probe.source == "usb":
        if count < len(plan):
            raise CameraMismatchError(f"setup needs {len(plan)} camera(s); {label}")
        found_usb = {serial_key(c.serial) for c in probe.cameras}
        missing = [
            c.serial for c in plan if c.serial and serial_key(c.serial) not in found_usb
        ]
        if missing:
            raise CameraMismatchError(
                f"camera serial(s) {missing} not connected; {label} (source=usb): "
                f"{sorted(found_usb)}"
            )
        if not pass_serial:
            log.warning("No SDK index order via USB: FlyCapture uses configured index")
        return _finish(plan, pass_serial)

    by_serial = {
        serial_key(c.serial): c.index
        for c in probe.cameras
        if c.serial and c.index is not None
    }
    missing = [
        c.serial for c in plan if c.serial and serial_key(c.serial) not in by_serial
    ]
    if missing:
        raise CameraMismatchError(
            f"camera serial(s) {missing} not connected; {label}: {sorted(by_serial)}"
        )
    for c in plan:
        if c.serial:
            c.index = by_serial[serial_key(c.serial)]
        elif c.index >= count:
            raise CameraMismatchError(
                f"camera {c.name or c.index!r} has no serial and index {c.index} "
                f"is not connected; {label}"
            )
    indices = [c.index for c in plan]
    if len(set(indices)) != len(indices):
        raise CameraMismatchError(f"two cameras resolve to one index: {indices}")
    return _finish(plan, pass_serial)

class FlirBonsaiBackend:
    """FLIR cameras recorded by one Bonsai process each.

    Args:
        probe: ``probe(driver) -> ProbeResult``; defaults to
            :func:`probe_cameras` with a 10 s timeout.
        runner_factory: Builds one runner per camera with the
            :class:`BonsaiCameraRunner` keyword arguments; defaults to that
            class.
    """

    acq_type = "video_flir"
    version = __version__

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        probe: Callable[[str], ProbeResult] | None = None,
        runner_factory: Callable[..., Any] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self._probe = probe or (lambda d: probe_cameras(d, timeout=_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S))
        self._runner_factory = runner_factory or BonsaiCameraRunner
        self._settings = FlirSettings()
        self._bonsai_exe = ""
        self._units: list[FlirUnit] = []
        self._plan: dict[str, CameraLaunch] = {}
        self._serials: dict[str, str] = {}
        self._preflight: dict[str, UnitResult] | None = None
        self._runners: dict[str, Any] = {}
        self._files: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        self._results: dict[str, UnitResult] = {}
        self._stopped: dict[str, UnitResult] | None = None
        self._acqdir = ""

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # configure / preflight

    def configure(
        self, settings: Mapping[str, Any], units: list[CameraUnitSpec]
    ) -> None:
        """Validate and store the settings and cameras.

        Raises:
            CameraConfigError: Unknown or invalid settings, invalid cameras, or
                no ``Bonsai.exe`` (:func:`resolve_bonsai_exe`).
        """
        self._settings = parse_settings(settings)
        self._units = parse_units(list(units), self._settings.n_cameras)
        self._bonsai_exe = resolve_bonsai_exe(self._settings.bonsai_exe)
        self._plan = {}
        self._serials = {}
        self._preflight = None
        self._results = {}
        self._stopped = None

    def preflight(self) -> list[UnitResult]:
        """Probe the cameras and resolve each one's launch index.

        Returns:
            Per camera ``ready`` (``extra``: probe source, resolved index,
            serial, and ``probe_serials`` when the probe has no index order)
            or ``missing`` (the probe message as ``error``); every
            camera ``failed`` (``bonsai_not_found``) when ``Bonsai.exe`` is gone.
        """
        driver = self._settings.driver
        if not Path(self._bonsai_exe).is_file():
            error = f"Bonsai.exe not found: {self._bonsai_exe!r}"
            log.error(f"flir_bonsai: {error}")
            self._plan = {}
            self._serials = {}
            gone = {
                u.name: UnitResult(
                    name=u.name,
                    ok=False,
                    state=UNIT_FAILED,
                    error=error,
                    error_code="bonsai_not_found",
                )
                for u in self._units
            }
            self._preflight = gone
            self._results = dict(gone)
            return self._ordered(gone)
        try:
            probe = self._probe(driver)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001  the probe must not break a run
            probe = ProbeResult(driver, error=f"probe raised {e!r}")
        source = probe.source if probe.source != "none" else "unavailable"
        at_index = {
            c.index: c.serial for c in probe.cameras if c.index is not None and c.serial
        }
        unordered = [c.serial for c in probe.cameras if c.index is None and c.serial]
        unordered_keys = {serial_key(s) for s in unordered}
        self._plan = {}
        self._serials = {}
        results: dict[str, UnitResult] = {}
        for unit, launch, error in self._resolve(probe):
            extra: dict[str, Any] = {"probe": source}
            serial = unit.serial
            if probe.source != "none":
                if launch is not None and launch.index in at_index:
                    serial = at_index[launch.index]
                elif unordered:
                    if serial_key(unit.serial) not in unordered_keys:
                        serial = ""
                    extra["probe_serials"] = list(unordered)
            if serial:
                extra["serial"] = serial
                self._serials[unit.name] = serial
            if launch is None:
                results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
                    name=unit.name,
                    ok=False,
                    state=UNIT_MISSING,
                    error=error,
                    error_code="not_connected",
                    extra=extra,
                )
                continue
            self._plan[unit.name] = launch
            extra["index"] = launch.index
            results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
                name=unit.name, ok=True, state=UNIT_READY, extra=extra
            )
        self._preflight = results
        self._results = dict(results)
        return self._ordered(results)

    def _resolve(
        self, probe: ProbeResult
    ) -> list[tuple[FlirUnit, CameraLaunch | None, str]]:
        """Launch plan per unit, or None with the reason it is missing."""
        driver = self._settings.driver

        def probe_units(units: list[FlirUnit]) -> list[_ProbeUnit]:
            return [_ProbeUnit(u.name, u.index, u.serial) for u in units]

        try:
            plan = resolve_camera_units(probe_units(self._units), driver, probe)
            return [(u, p, "") for u, p in zip(self._units, plan, strict=True)]
        except CameraMismatchError as e:
            group_error = str(e)
        missing: dict[str, str] = {}
        for u in self._units:
            try:
                resolve_camera_units(probe_units([u]), driver, probe)
            except CameraMismatchError as e:
                missing[u.name] = str(e)
        rest = [u for u in self._units if u.name not in missing]
        resolved: dict[str, CameraLaunch] = {}
        if rest:
            try:
                plan = resolve_camera_units(probe_units(rest), driver, probe)
                resolved = {p.name: p for p in plan}
            except CameraMismatchError as e:
                missing.update({u.name: str(e) for u in rest})
        out: list[tuple[FlirUnit, CameraLaunch | None, str]] = []
        for u in self._units:
            if u.name in resolved:
                out.append((u, resolved[u.name], ""))
            else:
                out.append((u, None, missing.get(u.name, group_error)))
        return out

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # start

    def start(self, target: CameraTarget) -> list[UnitResult]:
        """Launch one Bonsai per ready camera and wait for each first frame.

        Runs :meth:`preflight` first if it has not run. Cameras that failed
        preflight are not launched and keep their preflight result.

        Returns:
            Per camera ``recording``, ``failed`` (no first frame, or the launch
            itself failed) or ``missing``.

        Raises:
            RuntimeError: Called again while cameras are recording.
        """
        if self._runners:
            raise RuntimeError("flir_bonsai: start called while recording")
        if self._preflight is None:
            self.preflight()
        assert self._preflight is not None
        self._acqdir = target.acqdir
        self._stopped = None
        self._files = {}
        results: dict[str, UnitResult] = {
            name: r for name, r in self._preflight.items() if not r.ok
        }
        s = self._settings
        to_check: dict[str, Any] = {}
        for unit in self._units:
            launch = self._plan.get(unit.name)
            if launch is None:
                continue
            stem = camera_stem(target.basename, unit.label)
            self._files[unit.name] = [f"{stem}.avi", f"{stem}.timestamps.csv"]
            extra = self._extra(unit, launch)
            try:
                runner = self._runner_factory(
                    workflow=s.workflow,
                    acqdir=target.acqdir,
                    cam_basename=stem,
                    cam_index=launch.index,
                    driver=s.driver,
                    cam_serial=launch.serial,
                    bonsai_exe=self._bonsai_exe,
                )
                runner.start()
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001  one camera must not stop the rest
                log.error(f"flir_bonsai: {unit.name} could not launch: {e}")
                results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
                    name=unit.name,
                    ok=False,
                    state=UNIT_FAILED,
                    error=f"launch failed: {e}",
                    error_code="launch_failed",
                    extra=extra,
                )
                continue
            self._runners[unit.name] = runner
            to_check[unit.name] = runner

        errors: dict[str, str] = {}

        def check(name: str, runner: Any) -> None:
            try:
                runner.check_started()
            except BonsaiStartError as e:
                errors[name] = str(e)
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
                errors[name] = f"start check failed: {e!r}"

        threads = [
            threading.Thread(target=check, args=item, daemon=True)
            for item in to_check.items()
        ]
        for t in threads:
            t.start()
        for t in threads:
            t.join()

        for unit in self._units:
            runner = to_check.get(unit.name)
            if runner is None:
                continue
            extra = self._extra(unit, self._plan[unit.name])
            if unit.name in errors:
                self._runners.pop(unit.name, None)
                _safe_stop(runner, _STOP_TIMEOUT_S)
                results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
                    name=unit.name,
                    ok=False,
                    state=UNIT_FAILED,
                    error=errors[unit.name],
                    error_code="no_first_frame",
                    files=self._existing_files(unit.name),
                    extra=extra,
                )
            else:
                results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
                    name=unit.name,
                    ok=True,
                    state=UNIT_RECORDING,
                    files=list(self._files[unit.name]),
                    extra={**extra, "pid": getattr(runner, "pid", None)},
                )
        self._results = dict(results)
        return self._ordered(results)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # stop / close

    def stop(self, reason: str) -> list[UnitResult]:
        """Stop every recording camera and judge what it saved.

        A camera is ``stopped`` when Bonsai exited after the stop request and
        its timestamps file has data, else ``failed``: it did not exit, it
        exited before the stop (Bonsai exits 0 without recording), or the
        timestamps file is missing or empty. ``extra["returncode"]`` holds the
        exit code. Cameras that never recorded keep their earlier result.
        Calling it again returns the same results.
        """
        if self._stopped is not None:
            return self._ordered(self._stopped)
        log.info(f"flir_bonsai: stopping {sorted(self._runners)} ({reason})")
        runners = dict(self._runners)
        early = {name: bool(r.exited_unexpectedly) for name, r in runners.items()}
        threads = [
            threading.Thread(target=_safe_stop, args=(r, _STOP_TIMEOUT_S), daemon=True)
            for r in runners.values()
        ]
        for t in threads:
            t.start()
        for t in threads:
            t.join(timeout=_STOP_TIMEOUT_S + 2)

        results = dict(self._results)
        for unit in self._units:
            runner = runners.get(unit.name)
            if runner is None:
                prev = results.get(unit.name)
                if prev is None or prev.state in (UNIT_READY, UNIT_RECORDING):
                    results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
                        name=unit.name, ok=True, state=UNIT_STOPPED
                    )
                continue
            rc = runner.wait(timeout=_EXIT_WAIT_S)
            extra = {**self._extra(unit, self._plan[unit.name]), "returncode": rc}
            files = self._existing_files(unit.name)
            error, code = "", ""
            if rc is None:
                error, code = "Bonsai did not exit after the stop request", "no_exit"
            elif early[unit.name]:
                error = f"Bonsai exited before the stop (returncode={rc})"
                code = "exited_early"
            elif not self._timestamps_ok(unit.name):
                error = "timestamps file missing or empty"
                code = "empty_timestamps"
            results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
                name=unit.name,
                ok=not error,
                state=UNIT_FAILED if error else UNIT_STOPPED,
                error=error,
                error_code=code,
                files=files,
                extra=extra,
            )
            if error:
                log.error(f"flir_bonsai: {unit.name}: {error}")
        self._runners = {
            n: r for n, r in runners.items() if getattr(r, "is_running", False)
        }
        self._results = dict(results)
        self._stopped = results
        return self._ordered(results)

    def close(self) -> None:
        """Kill any Bonsai still running. Safe to call repeatedly."""
        for name, runner in list(self._runners.items()):
            if getattr(runner, "is_running", False):
                log.warning(f"flir_bonsai: killing {name} on close")
                _safe_stop(runner, 0.0)
        self._runners = {}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # helpers

    def _ordered(self, results: dict[str, UnitResult]) -> list[UnitResult]:
        return [results[u.name] for u in self._units if u.name in results]

    def _extra(self, unit: FlirUnit, launch: CameraLaunch) -> dict[str, Any]:
        extra: dict[str, Any] = {"index": launch.index}
        serial = self._serials.get(unit.name, unit.serial)
        if serial:
            extra["serial"] = serial
        return extra

    def _existing_files(self, name: str) -> list[str]:
        root = Path(self._acqdir)
        return [f for f in self._files.get(name, []) if (root / f).is_file()]

    def _timestamps_ok(self, name: str) -> bool:
        ts = Path(self._acqdir) / self._files[name][1]
        try:
            return ts.stat().st_size > 0
        except OSError:
            return False

def preflight(self) -> list[UnitResult]:
    """Probe the cameras and resolve each one's launch index.

    Returns:
        Per camera ``ready`` (``extra``: probe source, resolved index,
        serial, and ``probe_serials`` when the probe has no index order)
        or ``missing`` (the probe message as ``error``); every
        camera ``failed`` (``bonsai_not_found``) when ``Bonsai.exe`` is gone.
    """
    driver = self._settings.driver
    if not Path(self._bonsai_exe).is_file():
        error = f"Bonsai.exe not found: {self._bonsai_exe!r}"
        log.error(f"flir_bonsai: {error}")
        self._plan = {}
        self._serials = {}
        gone = {
            u.name: UnitResult(
                name=u.name,
                ok=False,
                state=UNIT_FAILED,
                error=error,
                error_code="bonsai_not_found",
            )
            for u in self._units
        }
        self._preflight = gone
        self._results = dict(gone)
        return self._ordered(gone)
    try:
        probe = self._probe(driver)
    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001  the probe must not break a run
        probe = ProbeResult(driver, error=f"probe raised {e!r}")
    source = probe.source if probe.source != "none" else "unavailable"
    at_index = {
        c.index: c.serial for c in probe.cameras if c.index is not None and c.serial
    }
    unordered = [c.serial for c in probe.cameras if c.index is None and c.serial]
    unordered_keys = {serial_key(s) for s in unordered}
    self._plan = {}
    self._serials = {}
    results: dict[str, UnitResult] = {}
    for unit, launch, error in self._resolve(probe):
        extra: dict[str, Any] = {"probe": source}
        serial = unit.serial
        if probe.source != "none":
            if launch is not None and launch.index in at_index:
                serial = at_index[launch.index]
            elif unordered:
                if serial_key(unit.serial) not in unordered_keys:
                    serial = ""
                extra["probe_serials"] = list(unordered)
        if serial:
            extra["serial"] = serial
            self._serials[unit.name] = serial
        if launch is None:
            results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
                name=unit.name,
                ok=False,
                state=UNIT_MISSING,
                error=error,
                error_code="not_connected",
                extra=extra,
            )
            continue
        self._plan[unit.name] = launch
        extra["index"] = launch.index
        results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
            name=unit.name, ok=True, state=UNIT_READY, extra=extra
        )
    self._preflight = results
    self._results = dict(results)
    return self._ordered(results)

def start(self, target: CameraTarget) -> list[UnitResult]:
    """Launch one Bonsai per ready camera and wait for each first frame.

    Runs :meth:`preflight` first if it has not run. Cameras that failed
    preflight are not launched and keep their preflight result.

    Returns:
        Per camera ``recording``, ``failed`` (no first frame, or the launch
        itself failed) or ``missing``.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: Called again while cameras are recording.
    """
    if self._runners:
        raise RuntimeError("flir_bonsai: start called while recording")
    if self._preflight is None:
        self.preflight()
    assert self._preflight is not None
    self._acqdir = target.acqdir
    self._stopped = None
    self._files = {}
    results: dict[str, UnitResult] = {
        name: r for name, r in self._preflight.items() if not r.ok
    }
    s = self._settings
    to_check: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for unit in self._units:
        launch = self._plan.get(unit.name)
        if launch is None:
            continue
        stem = camera_stem(target.basename, unit.label)
        self._files[unit.name] = [f"{stem}.avi", f"{stem}.timestamps.csv"]
        extra = self._extra(unit, launch)
        try:
            runner = self._runner_factory(
                workflow=s.workflow,
                acqdir=target.acqdir,
                cam_basename=stem,
                cam_index=launch.index,
                driver=s.driver,
                cam_serial=launch.serial,
                bonsai_exe=self._bonsai_exe,
            )
            runner.start()
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001  one camera must not stop the rest
            log.error(f"flir_bonsai: {unit.name} could not launch: {e}")
            results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
                name=unit.name,
                ok=False,
                state=UNIT_FAILED,
                error=f"launch failed: {e}",
                error_code="launch_failed",
                extra=extra,
            )
            continue
        self._runners[unit.name] = runner
        to_check[unit.name] = runner

    errors: dict[str, str] = {}

    def check(name: str, runner: Any) -> None:
        try:
            runner.check_started()
        except BonsaiStartError as e:
            errors[name] = str(e)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
            errors[name] = f"start check failed: {e!r}"

    threads = [
        threading.Thread(target=check, args=item, daemon=True)
        for item in to_check.items()
    ]
    for t in threads:
        t.start()
    for t in threads:
        t.join()

    for unit in self._units:
        runner = to_check.get(unit.name)
        if runner is None:
            continue
        extra = self._extra(unit, self._plan[unit.name])
        if unit.name in errors:
            self._runners.pop(unit.name, None)
            _safe_stop(runner, _STOP_TIMEOUT_S)
            results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
                name=unit.name,
                ok=False,
                state=UNIT_FAILED,
                error=errors[unit.name],
                error_code="no_first_frame",
                files=self._existing_files(unit.name),
                extra=extra,
            )
        else:
            results[unit.name] = UnitResult(
                name=unit.name,
                ok=True,
                state=UNIT_RECORDING,
                files=list(self._files[unit.name]),
                extra={**extra, "pid": getattr(runner, "pid", None)},
            )
    self._results = dict(results)
    return self._ordered(results)

def unwrap_cyclic(values: np.ndarray, period: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Unwrap a cyclic sequence of values by detecting rollovers.

    Args:
        values: 1-D array of values that cycle in [0, period).
        period: The period at which the counter resets.

    Returns:
        Monotonically increasing float array.
    """
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    if len(values) == 0:
        return values
    rollovers = np.diff(values) < -period / 2
    offsets = np.concatenate([[0.0], np.cumsum(rollovers) * period])
    return values + offsets

def decode_flycap_timestamp(raw: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Decode packed FlyCapture ``embeddedTimeStamp`` words to seconds in [0, 128).

    Args:
        raw: 1-D array of uint32 register values.

    Returns:
        Float seconds, still cyclic with a 128 s period (see ``unwrap_cyclic``).
    """
    raw = np.asarray(raw, dtype=np.uint64)
    sec = (raw >> np.uint64(25)) & np.uint64(0x7F)
    count = (raw >> np.uint64(12)) & np.uint64(0x1FFF)
    offset = raw & np.uint64(0xFFF)
    return (
        sec.astype(float)
        + count.astype(float) / _FLYCAP_CYCLE_HZ
        + offset.astype(float) / (_FLYCAP_CYCLE_HZ * _FLYCAP_OFFSET_PER_CYCLE)
    )

def load_camera_csv(path: str | Path, driver: Driver = "flycap") -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Load a Bonsai camera metadata CSV into a DataFrame.

    The CSV has no header and three columns: ``gpio_state`` (line status
    bitmask), ``timestamp_raw`` (camera timestamp as written) and
    ``frame_counter``. See the module docstring for the per-driver fields.

        driver: ``"flycap"`` or ``"spinnaker"``; both write the same column
            order, the driver is checked here and used for decoding.

    Returns:
        DataFrame with ``frame_index`` followed by the three CSV columns.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the file does not have three columns or the driver is
            unknown.
    """
    _check_driver(driver)
    path = Path(path)
    raw = pd.read_csv(path, header=None, dtype=np.uint64)
    if raw.shape[1] != len(CSV_COLUMNS):
        raise ValueError(

    raw.columns = pd.Index(CSV_COLUMNS)
    raw.insert(0, "frame_index", np.arange(len(raw)))
    return raw

def preprocess_camera_csv(
    path: str | Path,
    driver: Driver = "flycap",
    counter_bits: int | None = None,
    session_start_s: float | None = None,
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Load a Bonsai camera CSV and decode its timestamps.

    Steps:
      1. Load the CSV (``load_camera_csv``).
      2. Decode ``timestamp_raw`` per driver into ``timestamp_s``.
      3. Unwrap the FlyCapture 32-bit frame counter.
      4. Optionally shift timestamps so t=0 is ``session_start_s``.

    Args:
        path: Path to Bonsai camera CSV.
        driver: ``"flycap"`` (default) or ``"spinnaker"``.
        counter_bits: Frame counter width to unwrap. Default: 32 for FlyCapture,
            no unwrapping for the 64-bit Spinnaker ``FrameID``.
        session_start_s: If given, subtract this from all timestamps so session t=0
            is the first behavioural event rather than camera power-on.

    Returns:
        DataFrame with ``frame_index``, ``gpio_state``, ``timestamp_raw``,
        ``frame_counter`` and ``timestamp_s`` (seconds, monotonic, optionally
        shifted).
    """
    df = load_camera_csv(path, driver=driver)
    df["timestamp_s"] = decode_timestamps(df["timestamp_raw"].to_numpy(), driver)

    if counter_bits is None and driver == "flycap":
        counter_bits = 32
    if counter_bits is not None:
        df["frame_counter"] = unwrap_counter(
            df["frame_counter"].to_numpy(), bits=counter_bits
        )

    if session_start_s is not None:
        df["timestamp_s"] = df["timestamp_s"] - session_start_s

    return df

def detect_dropped_frames(df: pd.DataFrame, expected_fps: float) -> pd.Series:
    """Detect dropped frames: return True where gap to next frame exceeds 1.5× the IFI.

    Args:
        df: Preprocessed camera DataFrame with ``timestamp_s`` column.
        expected_fps: Nominal camera frame rate in Hz.

    Returns:
        Boolean Series aligned to df.index, True where a drop is suspected
        after that frame.
    """
    ifi = 1.0 / expected_fps
    dt = df["timestamp_s"].diff().abs()
    return dt > 1.5 * ifi

Decode the barcodes on one camera GPIO line to the values Bpod sent.

The line is sampled once per frame, so its edges are the frames where its level changes. Barcodes are found by their configured lengths (ttl-barcoder's stream decoder) with the frame interval as the sampling interval: a barcode starts at its first high frame, and the init/end framing is checked only when the init pulses span at least two frames. Without framing, a long high pulse can decode as a barcode; matching the values to Bpod's rejects it.

Args: df: Preprocessed camera DataFrame with timestamp_s and gpio_col, or a FlirCamera from load_session(..., load=True). barcode_config: The settings the barcodes were sent with (the session's barcodes:, or the task's barcode settings). None uses the ttl-barcoder defaults, with a warning. gpio_col: Column name holding the line status bitmask. line_bit: Bit of the barcode line in gpio_col (31 on FlyCapture; the Spinnaker bit depends on the wiring). inverted: The line reads low while the Bpod output is high.

Returns: (time_s, value) per barcode: half a frame before its first high frame. Empty, with a warning, when a bit is shorter than three frames: over random frame phases most such barcodes decode to wrong values (35 ms bits at 60 fps decode exactly about a quarter of the time).

Source code in src/msw_flir_bonsai/alignment.py 
def extract_camera_barcodes(
    df: pd.DataFrame | FlirCamera,
    barcode_config: BarcodeConfig | None = None,
    *,
    gpio_col: str = "gpio_state",
    line_bit: int = FLYCAP_BARCODE_LINE_BIT,
    inverted: bool = False,
) -> list[tuple[float, int]]:
    """Decode the barcodes on one camera GPIO line to the values Bpod sent.

    The line is sampled once per frame, so its edges are the frames where its level
    changes. Barcodes are found by their configured lengths (ttl-barcoder's stream
    decoder) with the frame interval as the sampling interval: a barcode starts at its
    first high frame, and the init/end framing is checked only when the init pulses
    span at least two frames. Without framing, a long high pulse can decode as a
    barcode; matching the values to Bpod's rejects it.

    Args:
        df: Preprocessed camera DataFrame with ``timestamp_s`` and *gpio_col*, or a
            ``FlirCamera`` from ``load_session(..., load=True)``.
        barcode_config: The settings the barcodes were sent with (the session's
            ``barcodes:``, or the task's barcode settings). None uses the ttl-barcoder
            defaults, with a warning.
        gpio_col: Column name holding the line status bitmask.
        line_bit: Bit of the barcode line in *gpio_col* (31 on FlyCapture; the
            Spinnaker bit depends on the wiring).
        inverted: The line reads low while the Bpod output is high.

    Returns:
        ``(time_s, value)`` per barcode: half a frame before its first high frame.
        Empty, with a warning, when a bit is shorter than three frames: over random
        frame phases most such barcodes decode to wrong values (35 ms bits at 60 fps
        decode exactly about a quarter of the time).
    """
    from ttl_barcoder.core.barcode_ttl import BarcodeTTL
    from ttl_barcoder.core.config import BarcodeConfig

    df = _frames_of(df)
    if gpio_col not in df.columns:
        raise KeyError(
            f"GPIO column '{gpio_col}' not found. Available: {list(df.columns)}"
        )
    if barcode_config is None:
        barcode_config = BarcodeConfig.default()
        logging.warning(
            "No barcode settings given: decoding camera barcodes with the "
            "ttl-barcoder defaults (%s)",
            barcode_config,
        )

    level = line_state(df[gpio_col].to_numpy(), line_bit).astype(bool)
    if inverted:
        level = ~level
    ts = df["timestamp_s"].to_numpy(dtype=float)
    if len(ts) < 2:
        return []
    frame_s = float(np.median(np.diff(ts)))
    if barcode_config.bit_duration_ms / 1000 < 3 * frame_s:
        logging.warning(
            "Camera barcodes not decoded: %.0f ms bits are shorter than three frames "
            "(%.1f fps). Send longer barcodes to this camera.",
            barcode_config.bit_duration_ms,
            1 / frame_s,
        )
        return []

    # Only level changes are edges: a line already high at the first frame has no
    # rising edge there, so no barcode can start at it.
    changes = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(level)) + 1
    edge_times = ts[changes].tolist()
    edge_levels = level[changes].tolist()
    found = BarcodeTTL(barcode_config).find_barcodes(
        edge_times, edge_levels, sample_interval_s=frame_s
    )
    return [(b.start_s, b.value) for b in found]

docs.title: msw_flir_bonsai.alignment.align_barcodes(bpod_barcodes, camera_barcodes, max_hamming=2)
docs.text:
Compute the camera-to-Bpod time offset using matched barcode pairs.

Matching is done by Hamming distance on the barcode integer values, tolerating up to max_hamming bit errors (handles partial/corrupted barcodes). The median offset across all matched pairs is returned for robustness.

Args: bpod_barcodes: (time_s, value) pairs from Bpod. camera_barcodes: (time_s, value) pairs from camera GPIO. max_hamming: Maximum bit-error count to accept as a match.

Returns: offset_s such that bpod_time = camera_time + offset_s.

Raises: ValueError: If fewer than 2 barcode pairs can be matched.

Source code in src/msw_flir_bonsai/alignment.py 
def align_barcodes(
    bpod_barcodes: Sequence[tuple[float, int]],
    camera_barcodes: Sequence[tuple[float, int]],
    max_hamming: int = 2,
) -> float:
    """Compute the camera-to-Bpod time offset using matched barcode pairs.

    Matching is done by Hamming distance on the barcode integer values, tolerating
    up to *max_hamming* bit errors (handles partial/corrupted barcodes).  The
    median offset across all matched pairs is returned for robustness.

    Args:
        bpod_barcodes: ``(time_s, value)`` pairs from Bpod.
        camera_barcodes: ``(time_s, value)`` pairs from camera GPIO.
        max_hamming: Maximum bit-error count to accept as a match.

    Returns:
        ``offset_s`` such that ``bpod_time = camera_time + offset_s``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If fewer than 2 barcode pairs can be matched.
    """

    def hamming(a: int, b: int) -> int:
        return bin(a ^ b).count("1")

    offsets = []
    for cam_t, cam_val in camera_barcodes:
        best = min(bpod_barcodes, key=lambda bc: hamming(bc[1], cam_val))
        if hamming(best[1], cam_val) <= max_hamming:
            offsets.append(best[0] - cam_t)

    if len(offsets) < 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Too few barcode matches ({len(offsets)}) to compute a reliable offset. "
            "Check GPIO recording and barcode timing."
        )

    offset = float(np.median(offsets))
    jitter = float(np.std(offsets))
    logging.info(
        f"Barcode alignment: {len(offsets)} matches, "
        f"offset={offset:.4f}s, jitter={jitter:.4f}s"
    )
    return offset

docs.title: msw_flir_bonsai.alignment.align_ttl_edges(cam_df, bpod_event_times_s, gpio_col='gpio_state', max_offset_search_s=60.0, min_matches=5, line_bit=FLYCAP_BARCODE_LINE_BIT)
docs.text:
Estimate camera-to-Bpod offset by matching TTL rising edges.

The sequence task and others pulse a Bpod BNC line at trial start/end. The camera records these as GPIO state changes. This function cross-correlates the two edge sequences to find the best time offset.

Args: cam_df: Preprocessed camera DataFrame. bpod_event_times_s: Trial event times (e.g. trial-start) in Bpod clock. gpio_col: Camera GPIO column name (line status bitmask). max_offset_search_s: Maximum |offset| to consider during search. min_matches: Minimum number of matching edges required. line_bit: Bit of the TTL line in gpio_col (31 on FlyCapture).

Returns: offset_s such that bpod_time = camera_time + offset_s.

Source code in src/msw_flir_bonsai/alignment.py 
def align_ttl_edges(
    cam_df: pd.DataFrame,
    bpod_event_times_s: Sequence[float],
    gpio_col: str = "gpio_state",
    max_offset_search_s: float = 60.0,
    min_matches: int = 5,
    line_bit: int = FLYCAP_BARCODE_LINE_BIT,
) -> float:
    """Estimate camera-to-Bpod offset by matching TTL rising edges.

    The sequence task and others pulse a Bpod BNC line at trial start/end.
    The camera records these as GPIO state changes.  This function cross-correlates
    the two edge sequences to find the best time offset.

    Args:
        cam_df: Preprocessed camera DataFrame.
        bpod_event_times_s: Trial event times (e.g. trial-start) in Bpod clock.
        gpio_col: Camera GPIO column name (line status bitmask).
        max_offset_search_s: Maximum |offset| to consider during search.
        min_matches: Minimum number of matching edges required.
        line_bit: Bit of the TTL line in *gpio_col* (31 on FlyCapture).

    Returns:
        ``offset_s`` such that ``bpod_time = camera_time + offset_s``.
    """
    gpio = line_state(cam_df[gpio_col].to_numpy(), line_bit)
    ts = cam_df["timestamp_s"].to_numpy()
    rising_idx = np.where((gpio[1:] == 1) & (gpio[:-1] == 0))[0] + 1
    cam_edge_times = ts[rising_idx]

    bpod_arr = np.asarray(bpod_event_times_s)

    # Search over candidate offsets = differences between all pairs of edges
    candidates = []
    for ce in cam_edge_times:
        for be in bpod_arr:
            candidates.append(be - ce)

    candidates_arr = np.asarray(candidates)
    candidates_arr = candidates_arr[np.abs(candidates_arr) <= max_offset_search_s]

    if len(candidates_arr) == 0:
        raise ValueError(
            "No candidate offsets within search range: check GPIO and event times."
        )

    # Histogram to find consensus offset
    hist, edges = np.histogram(candidates_arr, bins=int(max_offset_search_s * 20))
    best_bin = int(np.argmax(hist))
    offset = float((edges[best_bin] + edges[best_bin + 1]) / 2)

    matches = int(hist[best_bin])
    if matches < min_matches:
        raise ValueError(
            f"TTL alignment found only {matches} matching edges (need {min_matches}). "
            "Consider increasing max_offset_search_s or checking GPIO."
        )

    logging.info(f"TTL-edge alignment: {matches} matching edges, offset={offset:.4f}s")
    return offset

def workflow_path(name: str) -> Path:
    """Return absolute path to a bundled .bonsai workflow file by stem name."""
    p = WORKFLOW_DIR / f"{name}.bonsai"
    if not p.exists():
        available = sorted(f.stem for f in WORKFLOW_DIR.glob("*.bonsai"))
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Workflow '{name}' not found. Available: {available}")
    return p

docs.title: Bonsai subprocess isolation
docs.text:
Each camera runs in a dedicated Bonsai subprocess launched by BonsaiCameraRunner. The subprocess receives all parameters (workflow path, output directory, camera serial number, frame rate) as command-line arguments and writes frame timestamps to a CSV file.

Isolation means a crash in one camera's subprocess does not terminate the others or the main behaviour task. The Python layer monitors subprocess health via poll() and logs failures without raising into the task.

docs.title: FlyCapture vs Spinnaker backends
docs.text:
The backend is determined by camera hardware, not software configuration:

  • FlyCapture2 (Bonsai.PointGrey2 package): Chameleon3, Grasshopper3 (older USB3 Gen 1 models). Requires the FlyCapture2 SDK from Teledyne FLIR.
  • Spinnaker (Bonsai.Spinnaker package): Blackfly S, Oryx, and current-generation USB3/GigE models. Requires the Spinnaker SDK.

make_camera_client(config) reads the backend field of CameraConfig to select which BonsaiCameraRunner subclass to instantiate. Multi-camera rigs with mixed hardware use MultiCameraRunner, which fans commands out to one runner per camera.

docs.title: Workflow XML structure
docs.text:
Bonsai workflows are XML files shipped as package data under bonsai_workflows/. Each workflow defines a reactive pipeline: camera source (FlyCapture or Spinnaker node) → frame sink (VideoWriter) → timestamp sink (CsvWriter). Parameters exposed to the command line are declared as ExternalizedMapping nodes in the XML, which BonsaiCameraRunner populates when building the subprocess command.

To add a camera parameter (frame rate, resolution): add an ExternalizedMapping node in the Bonsai editor, update _build_cmd() in the corresponding runner class to pass the value as a named argument.

docs.title: Timestamp alignment
docs.text:
timestamps.py provides utilities for working with camera frame timestamps:

  • load_camera_csv(path, driver): reads the headerless Bonsai CSV as gpio_state, timestamp_raw, frame_counter
  • unwrap_cyclic(timestamps) / unwrap_counter(timestamps): corrects for hardware counter rollover in raw timestamp streams
  • preprocess_camera_csv(path, driver): loads the CSV and decodes the timestamps per driver (FlyCapture packed cycle timer, Spinnaker nanoseconds) into timestamp_s
  • detect_dropped_frames(timestamps, fps): identifies gaps larger than 1.5 frame periods, indicating dropped frames

alignment.py provides barcode and TTL-based alignment between camera timestamps and behaviour event times. extract_camera_barcodes() decodes the Bpod barcodes on a camera GPIO line (line_bit, 31 on FlyCapture) with ttl-barcoder's stream decoder, given the settings they were sent with. The line is sampled once per frame: a barcode starts half a frame before its first high frame, the init/end framing is checked only when the init pulses span two frames, and bits shorter than three frames are refused with a warning (most would decode to wrong values). align_barcodes() maps camera frame indices to behaviour trial timestamps via matched barcode events.

docs.title: MSW integration
docs.text:
In MSW tasks, camera acquisition is managed by the task framework:

from murineshiftwork.hardware.camera.client import make_camera_client
from murineshiftwork.logic.config import SetupConfig

config = SetupConfig.from_yaml("setups/rig-01.yaml")
camera = make_camera_client(config.cameras)
camera.start_recording(output_dir=session_dir)
# ... run task ...
camera.stop_recording()

The FlirBonsaiClient returned by make_camera_client wraps BonsaiCameraRunner and implements the CameraClientProtocol expected by TaskProcess.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or later
  • Windows 10/11 (the Bonsai workflows and camera SDKs are Windows-only)
  • Bonsai installed (the .exe is called by the runner)
  • A FLIR camera with either the FlyCapture2 or Spinnaker SDK installed

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
pip install msw_flir_bonsai

This installs the msw-flir console script and the Python API. It does not install the camera SDKs - those must be obtained from FLIR/Teledyne separately.

docs.title: FlyCapture2
docs.text:
• Download from the FLIR/Teledyne support page (search "FlyCapture2 SDK").
  • Install the SDK, then install the Python wrapper: PyCapture2 (a wheel is bundled in the SDK installer on recent versions, or available via the Teledyne download portal).
  • Cameras that use FlyCapture2: Chameleon3, Grasshopper3 (USB3 Gen1 models).

docs.title: Spinnaker
docs.text:
• Download the Spinnaker SDK from the Teledyne FLIR support page.
  • Install the SDK, then install PySpin (bundled in the Spinnaker Python installer).
  • Cameras that use Spinnaker: Blackfly S, Oryx, and current-generation USB3 / GigE models.

Verify SDK installation with:

msw-flir list-cameras --driver flycap
# or
msw-flir list-cameras --driver spinnaker

docs.title: Locate Bonsai.exe
docs.text:
The runner needs an absolute path to Bonsai.exe. Run:

msw-flir find-bonsai

This scans common install locations and prints the path. Either set the BONSAI_EXE environment variable to this path, or pass it explicitly when creating a BonsaiCameraRunner.

# Windows PowerShell (per-session)
$Env:BONSAI_EXE = "C:\Users\lab\AppData\Local\Bonsai\Bonsai.exe"

# or add it to your system environment variables for a permanent setting

docs.title: Verify with a test recording
docs.text:
Connect a camera, then run a 5-second test to confirm everything works:

msw-flir test-record --cam-index 0 --driver flycap --fps 30 --duration 5

Output is written to ~/msw_flir_test/ by default. You should see a .avi video file and a .csv metadata file (GPIO state, timestamp, frame counter).

# Check the CSV has the expected columns
python - <<'EOF'
from msw_flir_bonsai.timestamps import load_camera_csv
df = load_camera_csv("~/msw_flir_test/test/test__<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>/test__<YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS>__cam0.csv")
print(df.head())
print(df.columns.tolist())
EOF

Expected columns: frame_index, gpio_state, timestamp_raw, frame_counter. Pass driver="spinnaker" for Spinnaker recordings.

docs.title: First camera connection from Python
docs.text:
from msw_flir_bonsai.runner import BonsaiCameraRunner

runner = BonsaiCameraRunner(
    workflow="run-flir-flycap-1cam",    # or run-flir-spinnaker-1cam
    output_dir=r"D:\DATA\video",
    session="mouse001__20260524",
    cam_index=0,
    fps=60,                              # FlyCapture only; ignored for Spinnaker
    driver="flycap",                     # "flycap" or "spinnaker"
    # bonsai_exe not needed if BONSAI_EXE env var is set
)

runner.start()        # launches Bonsai subprocess, begins writing frames immediately
print(runner.pid)     # OS process ID for the Bonsai process

# ... wait, run behaviour task, etc. ...

runner.stop()         # asks Bonsai to finish; it flushes and closes its files
runner.wait(timeout=15)

This is the full acquisition lifecycle. For multi-camera setups see Usage.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: Common patterns for running cameras, preprocessing data, and aligning timestamps. For installation and first-run verification, see Getting started.

docs.title: Recording as part of an MSW session
docs.text:
The usual path: instead of driving the runner yourself, declare the camera in the rig's setup YAML under cameras: and run any camera-aware MSW task. MSW then launches Bonsai and records a video_flir acquisition (one .avi, one .timestamps.csv and one .camera.json per camera) alongside the behavioural data.

The .camera.json is written when the camera starts. It records the driver, the workflow, the camera index, the requested frame rate, the CSV column order and the timestamp encoding, so load_session decodes each camera without being told the driver. Recordings without it predate it and are read as FlyCapture.

One FlyCapture camera on a setup:

cameras:
  backend: flir_bonsai
  driver: flycap                  # default
  bonsai_exe: C:\...\Bonsai.exe   # or set the BONSAI_EXE env var
  cameras:
    - index: 0                    # from `msw flir list-cameras`
      name: top                   # optional label; appears in the artifact name

The full key reference and the per-backend bring-up checklist live in the main MSW docs (Setup config -> Cameras). The rest of this page covers driving the runner directly, which the MSW path does for you.

docs.title: Single camera
docs.text:
from msw_flir_bonsai.runner import BonsaiCameraRunner

runner = BonsaiCameraRunner(
    workflow="run-flir-flycap-1cam",
    output_dir=r"D:\DATA\video",
    session="mouse001__20260524",
    cam_index=0,
    fps=60,
    driver="flycap",
)

runner.start()
# ... behavioural task runs ...
runner.stop()
runner.wait(timeout=15)

bonsai_exe is optional when BONSAI_EXE is set in the environment.

docs.title: Multiple cameras
docs.text:
Each camera runs in its own subprocess. A crash in one does not affect the others.

from msw_flir_bonsai.runner import MultiCameraRunner

multi = MultiCameraRunner.from_config(
    n_cameras=2,
    driver="flycap",
    output_dir=r"D:\DATA\video",
    session="mouse001__20260524",
    fps=60,
)

multi.start()

# Poll until all processes exit (or add your own condition)
import time
while multi.any_running:
    time.sleep(0.5)

multi.stop()

from_config spawns one process per camera index (0, 1, ...) using the 1-cam workflow. The 2-cam workflow variants are legacy and not used here.

docs.title: Monitoring subprocess health
docs.text:
print(runner.is_running)   # False after crash or stop
print(runner.pid)          # OS process ID while running

print(multi.all_running)   # True if every camera is still active
print(multi.any_running)   # True if at least one is active
print(len(multi))          # number of runners

docs.title: Spinnaker cameras
docs.text:
Switch driver and workflow; everything else is the same. Do not pass fps for Spinnaker - set the frame rate directly in the workflow XML.

runner = BonsaiCameraRunner(
    workflow="run-flir-spinnaker-1cam",
    output_dir=r"D:\DATA\video",
    session="mouse001__20260524",
    cam_index=0,
    driver="spinnaker",      # fps not applicable here
)

docs.title: Preprocessing camera timestamps
docs.text:
The Bonsai workflow writes a headerless CSV with columns: frame_counter, timestamp_raw, gpio_state (optional).

FlyCapture timestamps are cyclic (128 s period) and may contain frame-counter rollovers. preprocess_camera_csv corrects both.

from msw_flir_bonsai.timestamps import preprocess_camera_csv

df = preprocess_camera_csv(
    "cam0__20260524_120000.csv",
    ts_cycle_s=128.0,    # FlyCapture rollover period; use np.inf for Spinnaker
    counter_bits=32,
)
# Columns: frame_index, timestamp_raw, timestamp_s, frame_counter, [gpio_state]

To zero timestamps relative to the first behavioural event:

df = preprocess_camera_csv(
    "cam0.csv",
    session_start_s=bpod_session_start_time,  # subtract this from all timestamps
)

docs.title: Detecting dropped frames
docs.text:
from msw_flir_bonsai.timestamps import detect_dropped_frames

dropped = detect_dropped_frames(df, expected_fps=60.0)
print(f"{dropped.sum()} dropped frames detected")

# View the frames where drops occurred
print(df.loc[dropped, ["frame_index", "timestamp_s"]])

detect_dropped_frames flags any inter-frame gap larger than 1.5 times the nominal inter-frame interval.

docs.title: Aligning camera time to Bpod
docs.text: Two methods are available depending on what GPIO data was recorded.

docs.title: Barcode alignment (preferred)
docs.text:
Use this when both the camera GPIO and Bpod BNC recorded the same periodic barcode pulses.

from msw_flir_bonsai.alignment import extract_camera_barcodes, align_barcodes

# Extract barcodes from the camera GPIO column
cam_barcodes = extract_camera_barcodes(
    df,
    gpio_col="gpio_state",
    fps=60.0,
    barcode_bit_duration_s=0.1,
)

# bpod_barcodes: list of (time_s, barcode_int) decoded from Bpod events
offset_s = align_barcodes(bpod_barcodes, cam_barcodes, max_hamming=2)

# Apply the offset
df["bpod_time"] = df["timestamp_s"] + offset_s

offset_s satisfies bpod_time = camera_time + offset_s. Up to max_hamming bit errors per barcode are tolerated; the median offset across all matched pairs is used for robustness.

docs.title: TTL-edge alignment (fallback)
docs.text:
Use this when barcodes are absent or too sparse but Bpod pulsed a BNC line (e.g. at trial start/end) that the camera GPIO recorded.

from msw_flir_bonsai.alignment import align_ttl_edges

# bpod_trial_times: list of trial-start times (seconds) in Bpod clock
offset_s = align_ttl_edges(
    df,
    bpod_trial_times,
    gpio_col="gpio_state",
    max_offset_search_s=60.0,
    min_matches=5,
)

df["bpod_time"] = df["timestamp_s"] + offset_s

This method cross-correlates rising GPIO edges with Bpod event times via a histogram search. It requires at least min_matches agreeing edge pairs.

Scan known Windows install paths and print the Bonsai.exe location.

Copy the printed path into your setup YAML under cameras.bonsai_exe, or export it as the BONSAI_EXE environment variable.
